test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**was**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence is describing a past situation, as indicated by earlier verbs like “had stayed” and “rang.”
 
• The subject here is "Mr. Sinha" — a **singular** noun referring to one person.
 
• To match both the **past tense** and **singular subject**, the correct form of the verb "to be" is "**was**".
 
• Other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• "Were" – plural form or used with "you"; not suitable for a singular subject.
 
• "Been" – past participle, used with auxiliary verbs like "has/had"; not correct alone here.
 
• "Is" – present tense; not appropriate in this past narrative.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *To my shock and dismay, one of my distant relatives, Mr. Sinha was__ standing with his suitcase.* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• "Was" is the past tense of "is" for singular subjects like he, she, or a name (e.g., Mr. Sinha).
 
• Always ensure verb tense and subject number agree with the context of the sentence.
